name: OpenCart
title: OpenCart SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on OpenCart: 9 of 43 services wired. Catalogue and search are not, so it is not usable for a store yet. What works, and why.
lede: OpenCart is the most constrained backend of the 26. Its core API is for order management, not a storefront: ten controllers, and none for products, categories or search. At 9 of 43, the connector is not usable for a store yet.
verdict: Not usable for a store yet. With catalogue and search unwired, the storefront has no products to show, and none of the ways it places an order is implemented either. OpenCart core ships exactly ten API controllers — cart, coupon, currency, customer, login, order, payment, reward, shipping, voucher — so 9 of 43 is the honest ceiling for that API, not a to-do list.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your OpenCart store

env.name: PUBLIC_OPENCART_API_URL
env.note: Your OpenCart store’s URL. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_OPENCART_API_KEY
env.note: The API user’s username, from System › Users › API in the OpenCart admin. See the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_OPENCART_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: An API session token to use instead of logging in. It belongs to one shopper’s cart session, and the connector never swaps it for another.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/opencart-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_OPENCART_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_OPENCART_ACCESS_KEY`, `PUBLIC_OPENCART_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_OPENCART_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: Create an API user under System › Users › API in the OpenCart admin; its username and key go in `PUBLIC_OPENCART_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_OPENCART_API_SECRET`.
howItWorks: OpenCart core’s API (`route=api/...`) is for order management, not for a storefront catalogue. The connector wires what it can: the cart, shipping and payment addresses and methods on the API session, and shipping rates. There is no product, category or search controller to call.
`api/order/info` has no ownership check at all — any API caller can read any order — so the connector quarantines it behind an admin-only method that a shopper-facing call can never reach.
limitations: Not usable for a store yet: without the catalogue and search, there is nothing for a shopper to browse.

No order can be placed. Placing an order (`route=api/order/add`) needs a customer, both addresses and shipping and payment methods on the API session, which the storefront’s checkout calls cannot supply; every way the storefront places an order is unsupported.
Catalogue: not wired — OpenCart core has no product or category API controller, so the storefront has no products to list.
Search: not wired — there is no search controller either.

The API username and key come from `PUBLIC_OPENCART_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_OPENCART_API_SECRET`. SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser, so every visitor can read them and use that API user’s order-management access.

faq.q: Can I run an OpenCart store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: No. The connector has no catalogue or search to show — OpenCart core has no API for them — and the storefront cannot place an order through it. At 9 of 43 services, it is not usable for a store yet.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to OpenCart?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/opencart-connector`, set `PUBLIC_OPENCART_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Why is OpenCart only at 9 of 43?
faq.a: Because that is what OpenCart core’s API offers. It ships exactly ten API controllers — cart, coupon, currency, customer, login, order, payment, reward, shipping and voucher — for order management, with none for products, categories or search. The Svelte Commerce maintainers have asked OpenCart’s maintainers whether a storefront REST API is planned for OpenCart 4.

openQuestion: Is a storefront REST surface planned for OpenCart 4, or is a custom extension the expected route?

api.surface: The connector calls the core API of OpenCart 3.0.x through the single entry point `/index.php`, naming each endpoint in the `route` query parameter (`route=api/cart/products`), and it does not work with OpenCart 4, whose routes differ.
api.auth: The connector posts the API user’s `username` and `key` to `route=api/login` and replays the returned `api_token`, which is a PHP session ID, as a query parameter on every `api/*` call, logging in again after 50 minutes; there is no Authorization header, and shopper sign-in is not possible because OpenCart has no customer login endpoint.

calls.what: `GET route=api/cart/products` to read the cart, `POST route=api/cart/add` with `product_id`, `quantity` and `option`, and `POST route=api/cart/edit` or `route=api/cart/remove` with the line’s `key`
`POST route=api/coupon` with `coupon` to apply a code
`POST route=api/shipping/address` and `POST route=api/payment/address` to put one address of each kind on the session
`GET route=api/shipping/methods` for the rates and `POST route=api/shipping/method` with `shipping_method` to choose one
`GET route=api/payment/methods`, and `POST route=api/payment/method` with `payment_method` to choose one
`GET route=api/order/info&order_id=` only through an admin-only method, never from a shopper-facing call

rules: Request bodies are form-encoded with PHP bracket notation, such as `option[11]=42`, because OpenCart’s controllers read only form posts and treat a JSON body as empty.

Failures come back as HTTP 200 with an `error` key, and an expired session never returns a 401, so the connector throws on any `error` key and treats `error.warning` on the cart and address routes as the expiry signal.

The cart, coupon, addresses and chosen methods all live in the one session behind the `api_token`, so a token supplied for a shopper is never refreshed or swapped for another, which would hand that shopper someone else’s cart.
OpenCart 3 has no route to remove a coupon, so the connector posts a code longer than the 20-character coupon column to `route=api/coupon`, which clears the stored coupon before rejecting the code.
No API controller takes `page` or `limit` or returns a count, so lists report only the size of the set that came back.
